cells.tense: You are here with the pen, in a connection you can still steer by picking it.
cells.act: keep the heading when it is contested
cells.ask: When the next pull away from this direction comes — a phone call that would reopen it, a doubt you'd normally re-argue — hold to the plan you already set, and don't touch it again.
cells.core:
With someone you know well, you can pick a direction and mean it. Two lives meeting can become one shared line you both steer, and it holds because you got there by feeling the thing through before deciding, not by reasoning to a verdict. The weight is real and needs no announcement; the people in it can feel the line stay put.

The endings that come with this are real — something closes so something else can open. Keep the heading when the next pull comes and don't relitigate it. Settling it once, early, is what lets the new place have air. When it's going well, it needs no proof.

You can live in the new thing instead of guarding the old one.
cells.sheetLine: You pick a direction, and it can stand without being explained.
cells.verb: merging with someone into a single shared current
cells.place: at the point where something has to end before the new one has air

cells.tense: You are already living in the merged future, bracing at a threshold no one has finished building.
cells.act: rest in the result of the tending
cells.ask: Pick something you and another person have already made — the arrangement that works, the routine that holds — and use it this week without improving it. Let it be finished enough. Stay with what is here instead of reaching for the next version.
cells.core:
You can decide a connection through what you can see for it, and when it's going well the dreaming comes after the feeling has been fully felt. What's happening now is that the glow is outrunning what's actually here. Your sense of where this is going is so far past the life it describes that the next stage has already been lived in your head, and the threshold you're braced at is still being built. The push to merge faster reads to the other person as a draft they keep being asked to sign before they've read it.

Let the result of what you've grown together be enough instead of the next version of it. The connection you already have is the one to be in. What's coming arrives at its own pace, and you meet it on foot rather than at a run.

The glow is yours. The timing isn't only yours.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door that has already closed behind you.
cells.act: list the pulls on you and mark which are yours
cells.ask: Put the connections pulling at you on one page — the ones still open, the ones that ended, the ones you're unsure about — and beside each, mark which pull is yours and which is someone else's direction you've been carrying.
cells.core:
Where a connection has to be decided, something in you has gone thin, and settling the question has stopped being available. You answer an old pull as if it were still asking, so the present gets only part of your weight. What this is about — two lives meeting and choosing one direction — isn't being made or refused by you. It isn't being reached. You're at a doorway that has already closed, answering from the far side of it.

Strengthen what you can see instead of pushing at the choice. Take in many things at once, plainly, without having to pick one — what pulls, what ended, what someone else's direction was. That discernment is the charge. When several truths are held without collapsing them, tomorrow has something to stand on, and deciding has somewhere to land.

One page is enough.

cells.tense: You are steering a merging that is already happening, and you have put the pen down.
cells.act: show someone the way you found
cells.ask: Think of someone who is where you were before you learned to choose a direction through feeling, and tell them once, plainly, how you did it. Not a speech. The single step you saw and followed, stated plainly, then their road is theirs.
cells.core:
Two lives meeting and choosing one shared line is what you do well here, and you don't call it deciding. The direction is being steered — the line held, the ending made, the new room entered — and your account of it says it just happened to you. What is at work is a clear decision made from feeling. What is on record is circumstance, and the people on the other side of it can feel the difference.

Go back to the simpler form: direction you can pass on. When someone asks how you knew, don't say you got lucky. Point at the passage you used, once, and stop there. The route you found is worth more to them than the result.

You didn't just drift into it.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that a specific old connection is already behind the person at Too Little; the record only gives under-expressing and past-anchored, so the core locates the door without saying what it opens onto or who is on the far side. The reader could reasonably say the two becoming one flow is in a living partnership, not in the choosing itself, so every cell keeps the acts aimed at bringing the full current to a clear choice rather than at any particular relationship. The asks survive being wrong because each one can be carried out on any person in any room, and the sentence that serves the writer more than the person is 'two streams, one flow,' which was cut everywhere it wanted to appear on glass.
